title: Microsoft Teams: express voice enrollment from meeting audio
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, enrollment defaults, licensing description and control paths and commands are supported. Minor corrections should make the action rating reflect a launched, default-enabled policy and acknowledge the checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-11-13T19:41:44.
Express enrollment creates a Teams voice profile from meeting speech rather than requiring a manually submitted recording.
claims.quote: For express enrollment, opt-in allows the Teams app to automatically capture users' voice data from Teams meetings and create and update their voice profile via their in-meeting speech.

claims.claim: Users opt in through Settings > Recognition in the Teams app.
claims.quote: Enrollment starts in the Teams app: users go to Settings > Recognition and, depending on how their Enterprise administrator has enabled the feature for them, opt in to either express enrollment or active enrollment.

claims.claim: Generating a voice profile from in-meeting speech typically takes a couple of meetings.
claims.quote: Generating a voice profile using in-meeting speech typically takes a couple of meetings.

claims.claim: The express-enrolled voice profile supports speaker identification.
claims.quote: PassiveVoiceEnrollment | Allows users to create their voice profiles via their voice data from Teams meetings for speaker identification, transcription, and voice isolation.

claims.claim: The profile supports transcription and improves identification of who spoke.
claims.quote: PassiveVoiceEnrollment | Allows users to create their voice profiles via their voice data from Teams meetings for speaker identification, transcription, and voice isolation.

claims.quote: Even if the feature is available, users still need to opt in to enroll their voice and face and create their voice and face profile before they can start using voice and face recognition

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -PassiveVoiceEnrollment Disabled disables express voice enrollment on the Global policy.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -PassiveVoiceEnrollment Disabled
Set Teams AI policy "PassiveVoiceEnrollment" value to "Disabled" for global as default.

claims.claim: An administrator UI for configuring PassiveVoiceEnrollment is not documented; the policy is PowerShell-only.
claims.quote: Searched: PassiveVoiceEnrollment admin center EnrollVoice. Opened voice-and-face-recognition and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy. The overview says: You can access this policy only through Microsoft PowerShell. No administrator UI for this policy found.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollVoice Disabled disables active voice enrollment on the Global policy.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollVoice Disabled
Set Teams AI policy "EnrollVoice" value to "Disabled" for global as default.

claims.claim: An administrator UI for configuring EnrollVoice is not documented; the policy is PowerShell-only.
claims.quote: Searched: PassiveVoiceEnrollment admin center EnrollVoice. Opened voice-and-face-recognition and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy. The overview says: You can access this policy only through Microsoft PowerShell. No administrator UI for this policy found.

claims.claim: New-CsTeamsAIPolicy creates a custom Teams AI policy.
claims.quote:
To disable active voice and face enrollment for specific users, Enterprise administrators can create and assign a custom meeting policy to the users:
New-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity DisableEnrollment -EnrollVoice Disabled -EnrollFace Disabled

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy applies a custom Teams AI policy to selected users.
claims.quote:
To disable active voice and face enrollment for specific users, Enterprise administrators can create and assign a custom meeting policy to the users:
Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity DisableEnrollment -Identity testuser@test.onmicrosoft.com

claims.claim: PassiveVoiceEnrollment operates independently of EnrollVoice, so disabling one does not disable the other route.
claims.quote: This setting can also be individually set to Enabled or Disabled and operates independently of EnrollVoice.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Both EnrollVoice and PassiveVoiceEnrollment must be disabled to turn voice enrollment off completely.
claims.quote: As an organization, you have the option to Enable Active enrollment (via EnrollVoice) and/or Express enrollment (via PassiveVoiceEnrollment) for your users. To turn off voice enrollment completely, make sure to set both parameters to Disable.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Organizations previously disabling EnrollVoice get a one-time state duplication into PassiveVoiceEnrollment at launch.
claims.quote: any organization that previously had EnrollVoice set to disabled will see a one-time manual state duplication so that both EnrollVoice and PassiveVoiceEnrollment will have the same state when launching this new functionality.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy reference describes PassiveVoiceEnrollment as starting May 2026.
claims.quote: Starting May 2026, there will be a new setting - PassiveVoiceEnrollment, which will allow users in your organization the ability to enroll their voice profile using their in-meeting audio.

claims.claim: The Copilot release notes list express voice enrollment under November 17, 2026.
claims.quote:
November 17, 2026
Teams
1. Express voice enrollment in Microsoft Teams [Windows, Mac]

claims.claim: The Copilot release-note entry names Windows and Mac.
claims.quote: Express voice enrollment in Microsoft Teams [Windows, Mac]

claims.claim: Previously enrolled users can still unenroll after administrators disable enrollment.
claims.quote: If Enterprise administrators disable enrollment after the user enrolled, the user still has the ability to opt out after.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After express enrollment opt-in, meeting voice data is collected on an ongoing basis.
claims.quote: If users opt to expressly enroll their voice and face profile from Teams meetings, that data will be collected on an ongoing basis

claims.claim: Meeting speech is used both to create and to update the voice profile.
claims.quote: For express enrollment, opt-in allows the Teams app to automatically capture users' voice data from Teams meetings and create and update their voice profile via their in-meeting speech.

claims.claim: Teams audio and video used for express profile creation are not retained after the call ends.
claims.quote: If users enroll via express enrollment, Teams audio and video used to create voice and face profiles aren't retained after the end of the Teams call.

claims.claim: The user's profile is removed immediately on unenrolling.
claims.quote: The user’s voice and face profile is removed right away if the user unenrolls from the feature.

claims.claim: A voice profile unused for one year is removed automatically.
claims.quote: In addition, a voice and face profile that isn't used for one year is removed automatically.

claims.claim: Voice data is stored in the Office 365 trusted compliance store.
claims.quote: Voice data is stored in the Office 365 trusted compliance store.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not use voice and face profiles to train models.
claims.quote: Microsoft doesn't use the voice and face profiles of users to train any models or for any other purposes other than providing the voice and face recognition feature in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Microsoft uses the profiles only to provide the Teams voice and face recognition feature.
claims.quote: Microsoft doesn't use the voice and face profiles of users to train any models or for any other purposes other than providing the voice and face recognition feature in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Voice Isolation stores an encrypted local copy of the voice profile on the device.
claims.quote: When a user also uses Voice Isolation on their device, a local copy of the voice profile is stored encrypted.

claims.claim: The local Voice Isolation profile copy expires after 14 days.
claims.quote: This copy of the voice profile expires after 14 days and is replaced with a new copy of the voice profile.

claims.claim: The expired local voice profile copy is replaced with a new copy.
claims.quote: This copy of the voice profile expires after 14 days and is replaced with a new copy of the voice profile.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Teams Rooms use enrolled voice profiles to identify individual speakers and attribute their contributions in transcripts.
claims.quote: Voice recognition: Uses an enrolled user’s voice profile to identify who is speaking in the room.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters
claims.claim: Recognition attributes enrolled Teams Room participants' contributions in meeting recaps and Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: When an enrolled user joins meetings from a Teams Room, their contributions are accurately attributed in transcriptions, meeting recaps, and Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: Blocking required Microsoft speech service endpoints can cause enrollment failures.
claims.quote: Why does voice enrollment fail with errors like “Couldn't capture your voice”? This can be caused by network restrictions blocking required Microsoft speech service endpoints.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft identifies *.speech.microsoft.com as the endpoint to allow-list for enrollment.
claims.quote:
Ensure the following endpoint is allow-listed:
*.speech.microsoft.com

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Users can delete their voice and face profile at any time.
claims.quote: Users can delete their voice and face profile at any time using the Teams desktop app, even if their Enterprise administrator has turned off enrollment after they enrolled.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot export end-user voice enrollment data.
claims.quote: No, data export is managed directly by end users. Admins don't have access to export voice and face data, giving users full control over their face and voice data and profiles.

claims.claim: Export of enrollment data remains under the end user's control.
claims.quote: Export of enrollment data remains under the end user's control and within the user experience.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Cloud
claims.claim: Learn says voice and face enrollments are available up to GCC but not GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: No, voice and face enrollments are currently available only up to GCC and aren't available in GCCH or DOD environments.

claims.claim: Users whose PassiveVoiceEnrollment policy is disabled cannot use express enrollment.
claims.quote: -PassiveVoiceEnrollment parameter value: Disabled | Users with this policy can't use or access the voice profile capture or enrollment.

claims.claim: Enterprise administrators manage enrollment through Teams AI policy PowerShell for users, groups or the whole organization.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can turn on or off voice and face enrollment for specific users, groups of users, or the whole organization. They can configure the feature using PowerShell.

claims.claim: The cited enrollment and policy pages do not name a required administrator role for setting the Teams AI policy or managing enrollment data.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams AI policy voice face enrollment admin role permissions enrollment status delete profiles navigation; Teams PowerShell Teams AI policy administrator role Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy permissions. Read enrollment overview and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy; no named role.

claims.claim: Allowing Teams Rooms to identify users with their enrolled profiles is a separate configuration from enrollment.
claims.quote: there's a separate configuration to allow Teams Rooms to utilize user voice and face profiles to identify who is in a meeting room.

claims.claim: Teams Pro Management Portal > Rooms > Settings > Recognition > Configure with device settings > Voice Recognition reaches the room voice recognition control.
claims.quote:
Log in to the Teams Pro Management Portal. Select Rooms. Select Settings followed by the Recognition tab. Enable Configure with device settings. Modify to the desired configuration.
Voice Recognition | Off

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity PolicyName -roomAttributeUserOverride Attribute configures voice-based identification of enrolled room users.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity PolicyName -roomAttributeUserOverride Attribute -roomPeopleNameUserOverride On
roomAttributeUserOverride: Attribute - Rooms users who have their voice enrolled will be attributed in the transcription.

claims.claim: The device-level Voice Recognition setting defaults to Off.
claims.quote: Voice Recognition | Off | Users with enrolled voice profile are identified with their voice when using this device.

claims.claim: Microsoft says meeting-policy-based room recognition configuration will be retired in the future.
claims.quote: Meeting policy-based configuration will be retired in the future.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends device-level settings for Teams Rooms recognition.
claims.quote: We recommend using device-level settings because meeting policy-based configuration will be retired in the future.

claims.claim: Room voice identification does not occur if transcription is not enabled in the Teams Meeting policy.
claims.quote: If transcription isn't enabled in the Teams Meeting policy, voice identification won't occur.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators can view end-user voice and face enrollment status in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can now use Teams admin center to view end-user voice and face enrollment status and manage enrolled data directly from the admin experience.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators can delete end-user voice and face profiles and enrollment data in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can also delete end-user voice and face profiles and enrollment data directly from the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The cited pages do not give a navigation path to the Teams admin center enrollment-status and profile-deletion experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center voice face enrollment status delete profile users manage users recognition. Opened voice-and-face-recognition, including Manage enrollment data in Teams admin center; it names the capabilities but gives no navigation steps.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center enrollment-data management capability does not change default feature availability.
claims.quote: This capability does not change default feature availability and enrollment behavior. Existing policies and end-user controls for voice and face recognition and enrollment remain the same.

claims.claim: Voice isolation is controlled with -VoiceIsolation on Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -VoiceIsolation Enabled
To prevent users with this policy from using voice isolation, use the following script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -VoiceIsolation Disabled

claims.claim: Learn also requires EnrollVoice or PassiveVoiceEnrollment to be enabled for voice isolation.
claims.quote: You must set the -VoiceIsolation parameter within the PowerShell CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and -EnrollVoice and/or the -PassiveVoiceEnrollment parameter within the CsTeamsAIPolicy cmdlet to manage whether your users can use voice isolation.

claims.claim: The enrollment overview instead says CsTeamsAIPolicy includes -VoiceIsolation, a documentation conflict the briefing explicitly reports.
claims.quote: The CsTeamsAIPolicy also includes the configuration for Voice Isolation -VoiceIsolation.

claims.claim: Teams AI policy replaces the previous EnrollUserOverride setting in CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can manage voice and face enrollment by using the CsTeamsAIPolicy. You can access this policy only through Microsoft PowerShell. It replaces the previous EnrollUserOverride setting in CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to review enrollment status, delete profiles and check voice isolation, but these controls have no table rows.
claims.quote: Review enrolment status for your users in the Teams admin center, and delete profiles where required; Check that voice isolation and room recognition settings still match your intent. The table contains only express enrollment, active enrollment and room recognition.
claims.fix: Remove the two After rollout checklist bullets beginning 'Review enrolment status' and 'Check that voice isolation'. Their factual descriptions can remain in Governance controls; those checklist instructions name controls absent from the table.

claims.claim: The action rating is prepare despite a launched change with medium risk and an enrollment policy enabled by default.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; status: "launched"; risk: "medium"; Microsoft Learn documents the policy as enabled by default, so decide whether to leave it on or turn it off with PowerShell.
claims.fix: Set action to 'act-now': the assessment scale assigns that rating to a launched medium-risk change that reaches users without administrator action and has an availability decision to take. Individual profile creation remains user-opt-in.
